subject: Unexpected EU region impact — recommended routing changes & validation request
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Ortiz <samantha@fintech.ai>, edgeops@acme-corp.com
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 07 Nov 2027 08:12:05 +0000
Subject: Unexpected EU region impact — recommended routing changes & validation request

Hi Samantha / Edge Ops team,

Quick update — our telemetry shows an elevated error rate (5xx) and connection resets for tenants routed to eu-west-1 between 07:55–08:05 UTC. We have a partial degradation in one of the peering clusters causing tokenization timeouts for streaming sessions and occasional 502/503 responses.

What we recommend right now (low-friction actions you can validate quickly):
- Switch traffic to the EU fallback endpoint: api.fallback.eu.redwood.ai (TTL-friendly, single CNAME) — this preserves latency for EU users and uses a different peering path.
- If you use our sidecar, flip the region_preference header to "region:eu-fallback"; for direct API calls, add X-Redwood-Region: eu-fallback in requests.
- Short-term model fallback: if you currently call redwood-large-1, fall back to redwood-medium-1 to reduce error amplification while we restore peering.
- Increase client retry backoff (recommended: 200ms -> 500ms exponential, max 3 retries) to avoid sharp retries during convergence.
- Optional: reduce DNS TTL to 60s if you control the zone; otherwise we can trigger an accelerated update on our side.

We attached the EU fallback playbook (eu-fallback-playbook.pdf) and a screenshot showing the most common error pattern (edge_error_500.png). Can you validate the fallback switch for one app by 09:00 UTC and confirm via reply? If you need us to make the change on your behalf, we can coordinate — tell us the service name and we’ll trigger a temporary redirect.

We will follow up with a brief post-incident note and a proposed remediation timeline once peering is confirmed stable. Sorry for the disruption — working on restoring normal service.

Thanks,
Naomi Feldman
Head of Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
naomi_feldman@redwood.ai
+1 415-555-0123

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>

Date: Sun, 07 Nov 2027 08:33:10 +0000
Subject: RE: Unexpected EU region impact — recommended routing changes & validation request

Looping Ops in — Laura/Rishi, can you confirm the following ASAP:
1) Is api.fallback.eu.redwood.ai bound to the same egress IP ranges? Short answer: no change expected for customer allowlists — fallback routes through our alternate peering fabric. I flagged INF-4821 in Jira (link below) for tracking; please confirm in the ticket with the final IPs.
2) Confirm model fallback mapping: redwood-large-1 -> redwood-medium-1 (we should enforce this from the gateway side for affected tenants if customers opt in).
3) Is there any per-tenant state that requires cache-warm up after switching endpoints? If so, list the endpoints and a suggested warm-up call pattern.

I will stand by to coordinate manual redirects for customers who ask us to perform the change.

Ben
Ben Carter
VP, Customer Success
ben_carter@redwood.ai

Jira: https://jira.redwood.com/browse/INF-4821

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>

Date: Sun, 07 Nov 2027 10:05:02 +0000
Subject: RE: Unexpected EU region impact — recommended routing changes & validation request

Hi Samantha — thanks for the quick check.

Short answers:
- No additional allowlist changes required for the fallback endpoint; the egress IPs are within our alternate peering ranges. Laura — please paste the confirmed IP block list into INF-4821 (cc'd).
- We're pushing a gateway-enforced model fallback for applicable tenants; that will be active in the next 15 minutes for sessions switching to eu-fallback.
- Cache warm-up: small warm-up (5 concurrent calls with the usual context) is sufficient for the majority of models. We will include a warm-up snippet in the runbook.

Samantha — we triggered a temporary redirect for payments-worker-eu and are seeing a normalization of requests on our side. Can you confirm you see improved success rates from your canary by 10:20 UTC? If yes, we will move to a wider redirect for your account and follow up with a short postmortem draft.

Next steps (post-incident):
- We will publish a technical postmortem and the timeline in INF-4821 by EOD (draft link attached: postmortem-draft-brief.txt).
- Ops will run the peering re-provisioning and validate in 2 hours; we'll provide a final ETA in the Jira ticket.
- If you prefer, we can schedule a 20-min sync call to walk through the mitigations and the proposed long-term remediation.

Appreciate the fast coordination.

Naomi
